reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the orders so I can compare them with the refunds Alpha reported.
Alpha reported three refunds, but I have not checked them against the ledger yet. I'll list the refunds recorded there and compare them with Alpha's handoff before paying anyone.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: order 260 for 8294, 263 for 8982, and 265 for 10903. All three refunded orders exist in the order list, so I have no concrete reason to hold. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 29089 matches my own check: orders 25692 + 20673 = 46365, less refunds 8294 + 8982 = 17276, gives 29089. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch has no refunds, and its net balance of 62075 matches orders 261 (32750) plus 264 (29325). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance, since cobalt has a refund on order 265.

Cobalt's net balance of 39438 matches my check: orders 262 (33488) plus 265 (16853) is 50341, less the 10903 refund, which gives 39438. Alpha's refunds match the ledger, and all three customers' balances agree with my arithmetic, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 29089 is recorded. Birch has no refunds, and its net balance of 62075 matches orders 261 and 264, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's net balance of 39438 matches my check. I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched my own check against the orders and the verified refunds, so the batch is complete.
